meta.name: Iris Smart Glasses
meta.tagline: Open-source monocular heads-up display glasses, built from scratch
meta.description: Iris is a reference product for Protoforge: lightweight glasses with a 640x400 micro-OLED heads-up display in the right eye, two-microphone voice capture, head tracking, a capacitive touch strip and a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) link to a phone. Every number in this file feeds a simulation somewhere in the workbench.
meta.author: Aleksander Norman

concept.problem: Glancing at a phone for directions, captions, notes or notifications pulls attention away from the world. Existing smart glasses are closed, expensive and impossible to learn from.
concept.vision: An all-day, sub-50 g pair of glasses that shows small, glanceable information in the corner of your vision, hears your voice clearly, and whose every design decision - circuit, optic, chip, frame and factory - is open and reproducible.
users: People who benefit from live captions

use_cases.title: Turn-by-turn walking directions
use_cases.narrative: The phone streams the next maneuver over BLE; Iris shows an arrow and distance, redrawing only when it changes.

use_cases.title: Live captions
use_cases.narrative: Iris captures speech with its two-microphone beamformer, streams audio to the phone for transcription and shows the returned captions.

use_cases.title: Glanceable notifications
use_cases.narrative: A tap on the temple wakes the display, a swipe dismisses; head-tilt gestures scroll.

use_cases.title: Teleprompter / speaker notes
use_cases.narrative: Notes scroll at a pace set by head nods or taps during a presentation.

constraints: Total mass at most 50 g, balanced between left and right temples
Must look like ordinary glasses from 2 m away
Hobbyist-buildable prototype: 3D-printed frame, 2-layer PCB, off-the-shelf modules
Path to volume: injection-molded frame, turnkey PCB assembly

needs.text: Wear it all day without noticing the weight
Last a full working day on one charge
Read text in the display comfortably at a glance
Be understood by voice in a noisy street
Never feel hot against the skin
Content stays stable when the head moves
Can be built by one engineer, then manufactured in volume

requirements.text: Total wearable mass shall be at most 50 g.
requirements.rationale: Mainstream smart glasses land near 50 g; ordinary frames are 20-35 g.

requirements.text: Battery life in the reference mixed-use profile shall be at least 8 h.
requirements.rationale: A working day with the display used about a third of the time.

requirements.text: Average system power in the reference profile shall be at most 80 mW.
requirements.rationale: Derived from R-002 with a 180 mAh cell and margin.

requirements.text: Horizontal field of view of the virtual display shall be at least 20 degrees.
requirements.rationale: Enough for two lines of 20 characters.

requirements.text: Angular resolution shall be at least 25 pixels per degree.
requirements.rationale: Small text stays legible; 60 ppd is roughly retinal.

requirements.text: The virtual image shall appear between 1 m and 3 m from the eye.
requirements.rationale: Reduces refocusing between the display and the world.

requirements.text: The eyebox shall be at least 5 mm wide.
requirements.rationale: Tolerates frame slip and different faces without losing the image.

requirements.text: Skin-contact surfaces shall stay at or below 41 C at 30 C ambient with the display on continuously.
requirements.rationale: Conservative margin under common 43 C limits for prolonged skin contact.

requirements.text: Microphone array directivity index at 1 kHz shall be at least 4 dB.
requirements.rationale: Rejects diffuse street noise relative to the wearer's voice.

requirements.text: PDM decimation filter stopband attenuation shall be at least 60 dB.
requirements.rationale: Keeps aliased ultrasonic noise below the microphone noise floor.

requirements.text: Head-orientation estimate error shall be at most 2 degrees RMS during normal head motion.
requirements.rationale: Head-locked or world-locked content must not visibly swim.

requirements.text: The 1.8 V rail shall droop by at most 50 mV on a display turn-on load step.
requirements.rationale: Protects the BLE SoC brown-out threshold.

requirements.text: Buck converter output ripple shall be at most 30 mV peak-to-peak.
requirements.rationale: Keeps the radio and IMU noise floor clean.

requirements.text: Battery-sense divider current shall be at most 2 uA.
requirements.rationale: An always-on divider must not drain the cell in storage.

requirements.text: The IRIS-DSP co-processor shall close timing at 50 MHz (critical path at most 20 ns).
requirements.rationale: Fixed by the PDM clock plan.

requirements.text: The IRIS-DSP co-processor shall fit in a 3000 standard-cell budget.
requirements.rationale: Small enough for a shared-shuttle or FPGA prototype.

requirements.text: All PCB nets shall be routed with zero design-rule violations.
requirements.rationale: Board is ready to send to a fab.

requirements.text: Design-rule check shall report zero violations.
requirements.rationale: Clearance and width rules match the fab's standard capability.

requirements.text: The PCB shall fit inside the right-temple pod with at least 1 mm margin.
requirements.rationale: Mechanical-electrical interface.

requirements.text: Molded frame walls shall have at least 1 degree of draft.
requirements.rationale: Allows clean ejection from the mold.

requirements.text: A full prototype frame set shall print in at most 8 h on a hobby FDM printer.
requirements.rationale: One overnight print per design iteration.

requirements.text: Unit cost at 1,000 units shall be at most 120 USD.
requirements.rationale: Supports a student-accessible retail price.

requirements.text: Automated pick-and-place of the main board shall take at most 60 s per board.
requirements.rationale: Keeps assembly cost low at volume.

requirements.text: A learned power policy should extend battery life by at least 5 % over the fixed policy.
requirements.rationale: Stretch goal: adaptive display/radio duty cycling.

requirements.text: The combiner shall clear the collimating lens by at least 0 mm (no interference).
requirements.rationale: Found by the Optics Lab in v0.3: an 18 mm lens 8 mm from a 45 degree combiner makes the parts intersect.

requirements.text: The frame shall have a structural safety factor of at least 2 under the wear load cases (5 N temple spread, 10 N bridge bend).
requirements.rationale: Frames are flexed every time they are put on; a factor of 2 on yield covers material scatter in printed PETG.

requirements.text: The PCB shall fit the pod in the worst-case tolerance stack, including cold shrink.
requirements.rationale: Nominal fit (R-019) is not enough; every part in the stack has a tolerance.

requirements.text: The display focus error shall stay within ±0.25 D over manufacturing tolerances.
requirements.rationale: Found by the Structures Lab in v0.4: a printed housing alone gives ±0.60 D, so v0.5 adds a threaded focus cell set at assembly.

requirements.text: The collimator RMS spot size shall be at most 26 µm (two display pixels) over the full field.
requirements.rationale: Keeps small text sharp to the corners.

requirements.text: Lateral colour should be at most 4.5 arcmin (two pixels) at the edge of the field.
requirements.rationale: Open goal: the moulded COP + PC achromat reaches 5.8 arcmin; the optimiser traded colour for sharpness.

requirements.text: Firmware RAM use shall leave at least 25 % of the SoC's RAM free.
requirements.rationale: Headroom for stack growth and features.

requirements.text: Firmware flash use shall leave at least 20 % of the image budget free (two update slots).
requirements.rationale: Over-the-air updates need two image slots.

requirements.text: Glasses-side caption latency (audio frame + Bluetooth round trip) shall be at most 100 ms.
requirements.rationale: Leaves most of a 400 ms end-to-end budget for speech recognition on the phone.

requirements.text: The PCB shall be manufacturable on a standard-tier fab service (zero capability violations).
requirements.rationale: Keeps board cost and lead time low.

requirements.text: The solder-paste stencil area ratio shall be at least 0.66 on every pad.
requirements.rationale: IPC-7525 area-ratio rule for reliable paste release; v0.5 moves to a 0.10 mm stencil (0.12 mm was 0.667, no margin).

requirements.text: The antenna port return loss shall be at least 10 dB across 2.400–2.4835 GHz.
requirements.rationale: VSWR ≤ 1.9 is the usual small-antenna target; v0.5 had no matching network (3.9 dB, VSWR 4.5). Verified by analysis on an ASSUMED antenna impedance — confirm with a VNA.

requirements.text: The antenna feed trace shall have a characteristic impedance of 50 Ω ± 5 Ω.
requirements.rationale: A 0.15 mm trace on the 0.8 mm board is ~95 Ω; v0.6 specifies a grounded coplanar waveguide feed.

requirements.text: The Bluetooth LE link to a phone 5 m away, worn on the head, shall close with ≥ 0 dB margin at 90 % availability.
requirements.rationale: Captions stream from the phone; head and body losses plus a Rayleigh fade margin are included.

requirements.text: The hottest exposed frame surface shall stay at or below 41 °C with the display always on (3-D conduction model).
requirements.rationale: The lumped R-008 model averages heat over the pod; the 3-D model found a 63 °C hotspot on the optics housing behind the display in v0.5.

requirements.text: The hottest frame surface shall be no more than 10 °C above the area-mean surface temperature.
requirements.rationale: Flags heat with nowhere to spread before it becomes a skin-temperature problem.

requirements.text: The spring-hinge spring shall have a Goodman fatigue safety factor of at least 1.5 over the usage spectrum.
requirements.rationale: Shigley's spring design examples use 1.5; v0.5's spring was 1.40 at the over-travel stop.

requirements.text: The spring hinge shall survive at least 13,140 open/close uses (12 a day for 3 years).
requirements.rationale: Usage spectrum from the Mechanisms Lab; Miner's rule on Shigley's spring allowables.

requirements.text: Opening the folded temple past the detent shall need 3–30 N·mm.
requirements.rationale: Provisional range: a detent you feel but can open with one hand — confirm with a user test.

requirements.text: One frame size shall fit at least 30 % of adults (50 % women) on every fit rule: pupil distance, temple length and clamp force.
requirements.rationale: ANSUR II population model. v0.5 fit nobody: the rigid front clamped too hard, and the original spring hinge opened at 0.08 N, too loose.

requirements.text: Nose-pad contact pressure shall stay at or below 4.3 kPa.
requirements.rationale: About 32 mmHg capillary closing pressure (Landis 1930), a typical sustained-pressure limit for skin.

requirements.text: At least 85 % of wearers shall see the whole image without adjustment.
requirements.rationale: A fixed 6 mm eyebox must sit where most pupils are; v0.5 centred it 2.6 mm too far out (60 %).

requirements.text: Captions should reach 1.5 : 1 contrast against a 5,000 cd/m² sunlit street.
requirements.rationale: Outdoor legibility; needs a tinted lens or a brighter display — kept as an open goal.

requirements.text: Reliability over 2 years (8 h a day, 12 hinge cycles a day) shall be at least 90 %, counting a battery below 80 % capacity as a failure.
requirements.rationale: The Reliability Lab found the 180 mAh cell's cycle wear-out dominates (76 % in v0.5).

requirements.text: The parts-count MTBF of the electronics shall be at least 1,000,000 h (typical failure rates).
requirements.rationale: Random-failure budget; replace typical rates with supplier data before DVT.

requirements.text: The DVT plan shall demonstrate R = 0.9 at 90 % confidence with no more than 40 product units.
requirements.rationale: Keeps the design-verification build affordable for a small team.

requirements.text: Production-validation exit shall be within 52 weeks at 80 % confidence.
requirements.rationale: Commit externally to the P80 of the schedule Monte Carlo, not the most-likely plan.

requirements.text: Gross margin shall be at least 50 % at the stated retail price and target quantity.
requirements.rationale: Typical hardware margin floor that funds support, returns and the next product.

requirements.text: Every subsystem should reach technology readiness level 6 by the critical design review.
requirements.rationale: Most subsystems have analysis evidence only — building the EVT prototype is what raises them. Kept as an open goal.

subsystems.name: Display & optics
subsystems.description: Micro-OLED, collimating lens and a 45 degree partially-reflective combiner in the right lens.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.description: LiPo cell in the left temple, USB-C charging, high-efficiency buck to 1.8 V, battery sensing.

subsystems.name: Compute & radio
subsystems.description: BLE system-on-chip running firmware, talking to the phone app.

subsystems.name: Voice capture
subsystems.description: Two PDM MEMS microphones in an endfire pair along the right temple with a differential beamformer.

subsystems.name: Sensing & head tracking
subsystems.description: 6-axis IMU fused with a complementary filter; capacitive touch strip on the temple.

subsystems.name: IRIS-DSP co-processor
subsystems.description: Optional custom digital block: PDM decimation FIR and touch-gesture state machine, prototyped on FPGA, taped out on a shared shuttle.

subsystems.name: Main PCB
subsystems.description: 58 x 10 mm 2-layer board in the right-temple pod.

subsystems.name: Frame & enclosures
subsystems.description: Parametric front, temples and pods; 3D-printed for prototypes, injection-molded for volume.

subsystems.name: Firmware & power policy
subsystems.description: Display/radio scheduling, learned power policy, gesture handling.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing & assembly
subsystems.description: PCB assembly service, molded frame, final assembly and test.

interfaces.description: Display command/pixel link over a 24-pin FPC through the hinge.
Two microphones share a PDM clock, left/right on one data line.
IMU and touch controller on a 400 kHz I2C bus.
1.8 V core rail from the buck; VBAT sense to an ADC pin.
3.3 V display rail enabled by a GPIO load switch.
Board slides into pod rails; USB-C aligned to rear opening.
Optics module screws to the right rim; combiner sits in front of the right lens.
Heat from the pod spreads into the temple shell and the air.
Co-processor streams 16 kHz PCM frames and gesture events.

risks.mitigation: Cell with protection circuit, charger with thermistor input, 4.2 V CV limit, crush-resistant pod.
Large bend radius, strain relief, 20k-cycle fold test in DVT.

risks.cause: Continuous display use in hot weather
risks.mitigation: Thermal model in the Power lab, firmware thermal throttling at 39 C board temperature.
Kinematic mount with alignment pins, 5 mm eyebox margin.

risks.failure_mode: Port blocked by sweat or dust
risks.mitigation: Acoustic mesh, port on the lower edge, self-test comparing the two mic levels.

risks.failure_mode: Dropouts when the phone is in a pocket
risks.mitigation: Antenna at the outer edge of the pod, keep-out zone, range test.
Minimum 5 mm rim, fillets, PC material for volume.
Qualify a second display with the same FPC pinout; keep optics parametric.
